cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: length of the coupon period containing settlement, semiannual, actual/actual
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 181. Setup serials are the dates Microsoft's page prints: 40568 = 2011-01-25 (settlement), 40862 = 2011-11-15 (maturity), frequency 2 (semiannual), basis 1 (actual/actual). Counting coupon dates back from maturity in six-month steps gives 2011-11-15, 2011-05-15, 2010-11-15, so the settlement date falls in the coupon period 2010-11-15 to 2011-05-15. On basis 1 the length of that period is the actual day count from 2010-11-15 to 2011-05-15, which Python date subtraction gives as 181 days

cases.description: The same bond on the US (NASD) 30/360 basis instead of actual/actual
cases.expected_note: On any 30/360 basis a year is exactly 360 days, so a semiannual coupon period is 360/2 = 180 days regardless of the calendar -- one day fewer than the actual/actual 181 for this particular period. This case discriminates the basis argument, which the documented example alone does not

cases.description: A frequency of 3, which is not one of the permitted values
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If frequency is any number other than 1, 2, or 4, COUPDAYS returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If basis < 0 or if basis > 4, COUPDAYS returns the #NUM! error value."
